title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Finance (Tenure-Track) - John Chambers College of Business &
description:
The Department of Finance at John Chambers College of Business
& Economics, West Virginia University, invites qualified
applicants for a tenure-track position at the Assistant or
Associate Professor level to teach courses in the department's Risk
Management and Insurance program. Candidates hired at the rank of
associate professor will be considered for the position of Ernest
L. Hogan Chair of Life Insurance. This is a full-time, 9-month,
benefits-eligible appointment with an anticipated start date in
Fall 2027, with the possibility of a Spring 2027 start date.

Primary Responsibilities

Teach courses at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral
levels focused primarily on insurance-related topics but will
include other topics in finance and related disciplines.
Develop and implement innovative teaching methods to enhance
student engagement and learning outcomes.
Supervise and mentor doctoral students, including serving on
dissertation committees.
Develop a strong research program with the potential to publish
in high-quality academic journals.
Maintain an active research pipeline that contributes to the
advancement of the field of Finance.
Actively contribute to departmental, college, and university
service initiatives, especially those related to the Risk
Management and Insurance area.
Engage in program development, student mentoring, and other
academic activities that support the institution's mission.

Qualifications :

A Ph.D. in Finance or a closely related field (e.g., Economics)
is required.
Possess a strong research pipeline and demonstrate potential to
publish in high-quality academic journals. Candidates at the
Associate Professor level must have a track record of high-level
research published in well-regarded journals.
A teaching record that demonstrates excellence in the
classroom.
A strong commitment to service and engagement in academic and
professional communities.
All qualifications must be met by the time of appointment.

Application Process

Applicants should submit the following items electronically via the
WVU Faculty Jobs Board at https://careers.wvu.edu/career-opportunities
.

A letter of interest.
Curriculum vitae.
Evidence of teaching effectiveness (e.g., course evaluations,
sample syllabi).
A sample of scholarly work (e.g., publication or working
paper).
Contact information for three references.

Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until
the position is filled. We plan to attend the ARIA conference to
speak with potential candidates. For specific questions, please
contact Dr. Ann Marie Hibbert, Department Chair, at amhibbert@mail.wvu.edu .

About the College

The John Chambers College of Business & Economics is
AACSB-accredited and housed in the state-of-the-art Reynolds Hall,
located in Morgantown, WV. The college offers a dynamic learning
environment with undergraduate, master's, and doctoral programs in
a range of disciplines. For more information, visit https://business.wvu.edu .

West Virginia University is a place of purpose and community. We
take pride in our profound impact on the state of West Virginia and
are committed to the personal and professional growth of our
employees.

From the groundbreaking R1 research at our flagship campus in

At WVU, you will discover a supportive community that champions

Join us at West Virginia University, where your work will make a
